messages:
Rachel Parker: Hi People Ops — quick q: I was on parental LOA 2024-11-28 to 2024-12-12 and missed the year-end 2-day mandatory shutdown. My PTO balance shows I hit the carryover cap and the system dropped 2 days. Can we request an exception to carry those 2 days forward? I need to use them as partial days in Q1 for appointments. Thanks.
Marin (People Ops): Hey Rachel — sorry for the hassle. The standard carryover cap typically applies, but we do approve exceptions when an approved LOA overlaps the year-end shutdown. We’ll need a formal exception request filed in the HR portal with your LOA dates and manager sign-off so Payroll can consider it.
Sam Ellis: +1 from me — I support the exception. We had coverage on the team while Rachel was out. @Marin (People Ops) please note my approval. :thumbsup:
payroll-bot: Reminder: Year-end accrual cutoff was 2024-12-31 23:59 UTC. Exception requests submitted after payroll cutoff require People Ops escalation and may take longer. See https://intranet.redwood/people/pto-carryover
Marin (People Ops): Thanks @Sam. Rachel, when you file the ticket include the LOA approval PDF (or HR LOA record) and any medical note if applicable. Subject the ticket "Carryover exception request" and include manager approval text. Example ticket body you can copy/paste:
```
Subject: Carryover exception request — Rachel Parker
LOA dates: 2024-11-28 to 2024-12-12
Requested carryover: 2 days (to be used as 0.5-day partials in Q1)
Manager approval: Sam Ellis (sam@redwood.com)
Reason: Parental LOA overlapped year-end shutdown
Attachments: LOA approval PDF
```
Marin (People Ops): Once you create the ticket I’ll route it to Payroll + Benefits. Typical turnaround 3–7 business days; we can request expedited handling for payroll adjustments but that’s evaluated case-by-case.
Rachel Parker: Filing now — quick follow-up: if approved, can those two days be split into four half-days? I have recurring doctor appointments and would prefer 0.5-day entries.
Marin (People Ops): Yes, if the exception is approved partial-day usage is allowed. Please make sure you log 0.5-day entries in the PTO calendar and get manager approval for each partial-day request.
Sam Ellis: Approved for partials from my side. Also, if you need coverage we can do a shift swap internally — ping #eng-oncall and we’ll coordinate.
Rachel Parker: Filed ticket #2024-786 (link: https://hr.redwood/tickets/2024-786). Attached LOA doc. Thanks everyone :pray:
payroll-bot: Ticket #2024-786 received. Estimated response time: 5 business days.
Marin (People Ops): I see the ticket and routed it to Payroll. One note: if Payroll denies an exception they sometimes offer a pro-rated payout for contractors only; for full-time employees the usual remedy is an approved carryover, not a payout. I’ll confirm definitive outcome in the ticket.
Rachel Parker: Understood — appreciate the quick responses and the help coordinating this.
Marin (People Ops): Will post the payroll decision here when it arrives. In the meantime, log the intended partial days as tentative in the calendar so managers can see coverage needs.
